journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component traps focus inside the calendar popup when shown, preventing the Tab key from moving focus to the next field. This occurs because the Vanilla Calendar Pro library's focus trapping is enabled by default.
plan.repair_strategy: Disable focus trapping in the Vanilla Calendar Pro instance by setting the `trapFocus` option to false in the calendar options passed to the Calendar constructor.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab will move focus from the departure date field to the passengers field as expected, allowing seamless keyboard navigation through the form.
functional_risks: Disabling focus trapping may allow focus to leave the calendar accidentally when it is open, but the datepicker component's outside dismissers (on focusin and pointerdown) will hide the calendar when focus leaves, mitigating this risk.

If the VCP library relies on focus trapping for internal keyboard navigation (e.g., arrow keys within the calendar), this change could disrupt those interactions. However, the datepicker component's primary functionality (date selection via mouse or Enter) should remain unaffected.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field.
Verify that the calendar still functions correctly for date selection via mouse and keyboard (arrow keys, Enter, etc.).
Verify that the calendar hides when clicking outside or pressing Escape (as per the regression guard 'Escape still closes the calendar').

plan.root_cause: The Vanilla Calendar Pro (VCP) calendar instance traps focus when the datepicker popover is shown, preventing the Tab key from moving focus to the next form field. The keydown event on the departure input has defaultPrevented set to true, indicating that VCP's internal keyboard handler cancels the default tab navigation. The VCP option to disable focus trapping is likely named 'trapFocus' or 'focusTrap', but the exact property name is not documented in the Bootstrap source. Previous attempts setting only 'trapFocus: false' did not resolve the issue, suggesting the option might be named differently or both options are needed.
plan.repair_strategy: Disable focus trapping in the VCP calendar by setting both 'trapFocus: false' and 'focusTrap: false' in the calendar options passed to the Calendar constructor. This covers possible naming variations in the VCP library. The options are added after 'themeAttrDetect' in the calendarOptions object.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab from the departure date field will move focus to the passengers field as expected, allowing seamless keyboard navigation through the form. The datepicker popover will still open on focus and can be closed with Escape (regression guard).
functional_risks: Disabling focus trapping may allow focus to leave the calendar accidentally when it is open, but the datepicker component's outside dismissers (on focusin and pointerdown) will hide the calendar when focus leaves, mitigating this risk.

If the VCP library relies on focus trapping for internal keyboard navigation (e.g., arrow keys within the calendar), this change could disrupt those interactions. However, the datepicker component's primary functionality (date selection via mouse or Enter) should remain unaffected.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field.
Verify that the calendar still functions correctly for date selection via mouse and keyboard (arrow keys, Enter, etc.).
Verify that the calendar hides when clicking outside or pressing Escape (as per the regression guard 'Escape still closes the calendar').
